subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@acme.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned while we size Dedicated for ACME: 

Call recap (high level)
- ACME will prioritize low-latency inference for conversational assistants and on-demand summarization.
- Current production traffic (pilot): ~120 TPS at peak for short-chat endpoint; expected growth to ~600 TPS within 6–9 months.
- Token mix: ~70% short prompts (avg prompt+response ~60 tokens), 30% long-form summarization (avg ~1.2k tokens).
- Hard SLO: P95 latency < 350ms for chat; throughput target supports 600 TPS at steady state.

Initial sizing ask from you: preferred GPU type, concurrency guidance, and a committed configuration we can price/contract.

Attachments: I see the workload summary you shared earlier (ACME_workload_summary.xlsx) — thanks for that. I’ll attach our initial pricing/estimate doc after we validate a few items below.

Quick clarifying questions (to confirm before we lock on a config):
1) Will ACME accept model quantization to int8/4-bit for the chat endpoint (we usually recommend int8 for cost/throughput gains)?
2) Do you plan to pin to a single model family (e.g., Llama 3 13B) or need multi-model routing (mix of larger/smaller variants for quality vs cost)?
3) Any region constraints (must run in us-west vs multi-region for DR)?

Proposed next steps
- Claire: confirm answers to the 3 clarifying questions and share any updated traffic forecast spreadsheet.
- Redwood (me + SE): we’ll produce a Dedicated sizing doc with: recommended GPU SKUs, node counts for baseline vs peak, concurrency/tokens assumptions, and a draft pricing attachment (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf).
- Schedule a quick 30-min sizing review with Aditya to validate assumptions.

I’ve tentatively penciled in Tue 5/4 10:00am PT for a sizing review. Does that work?

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

[attachment stub: ACME_workload_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@acme.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps

Thanks Rafael — quick answers below, and appreciate the clear plan.

Answers:
1) Quantization: yes, ACME is open to int8 for the chat endpoint as long as we validate quality on our key prompt set. For long-form summarization we prefer float16 for now.
2) Model routing: we plan to pin chat to a 13B family (production) and allow occasional routing to a 70B variant for high-quality summaries. Ideally Redwood can handle mixed routing with fallback to the 13B when dedicated capacity for 70B is exhausted.
3) Region: primary in us-west (AWS us-west-2) for latency; DR in us-east-1 is optional but not required for initial commit.

Traffic: we confirmed the forecast with product — peak is 600 TPS in 9 months (conservative), median 220 TPS today. Token mix is as you noted (70% short, 30% long) — I attached an updated spreadsheet.

We can do Tue 5/4 10am PT for the sizing review — invite Aditya if he can make it.

Claire Huang
Director, AI Platforms | ACME Corp
claire.huang@acme.io

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@acme.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps

Great — thanks for the quick confirmations and the updated spreadsheet, Claire. Based on the traffic profile and token mix you confirmed, here are our recommended Dedicated sizing and notes: 

High-level recommendation (baseline -> peak)
- Baseline (current median ~220 TPS): 4 nodes of NVIDIA H100 80GB (A100 alternative if H100 not available) running model family Llama-3-13B quantized to int8 for chat, and Llama-3-70B float16 reserved for on-demand high-quality summaries via burst pool.
- Peak (600 TPS target): scale to 10 H100 nodes; autoscaling policy for burst to an additional 4 nodes in high-traffic windows.

Concurrency and worker sizing
- For 13B int8 chat: projected concurrency per GPU ~12 concurrent requests at low-latency (tight batching), estimated throughput per GPU ~55–70 TPS depending on batching and prompt length.
- For 70B float16: lower concurrency (2–3 concurrent requests per GPU) — use a separate pool or fallback routing.

Token assumptions used in these estimates
- Short-chat: avg 60 tokens (70% of calls)
- Long summarization: avg 1,200 tokens (30% of calls)

Storage / KV cache note
- We recommend enabling prefix KV caching for chat to reduce repeated context cost; this typically improves effective throughput by ~15–25% for repeat prompts (we can validate with your prompt set).

Pricing and contract
- Attached is an initial pricing workbook (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf) with committed node examples and a burst policy. This is a draft — we can adjust commitments/term length to match ACME procurement goals.

Next steps / action items
1) Aditya + ACME SEs: quick sizing review Tue 5/4 10:00am PT (30 min) — validate concurrency assumptions and model routing.
2) Claire: confirm willingness to commit to an initial 6-month reserved baseline (we’ll provide a discount schedule in the attached).
3) Redwood: we’ll produce a finalized capacity diagram and a short SLA addendum for Dedicated.

I attached the draft pricing doc and included a short lane-by-lane node estimate in the file.

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@acme.io>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps

Claire / Rafael — quick SE notes ahead of Tue’s call (validated against the spreadsheet Claire shared):

1) GPU SKU tradeoffs
- H100 80GB: best for large-model throughput and KV cache residency for 70B family. If ACME requires more aggressive concurrency for 70B, consider moving some 70B inference to a dedicated float16 pool with multiple H100s.
- A100 80GB (if H100 not available): can meet latency targets for 13B int8 but expect ~15% lower throughput vs H100 for long-form summarization.

2) Concurrency & batching knobs to tune in the pilot
- Target low-latency concurrency for chat endpoints at 8–12 concurrent requests/GPU with dynamic batching window of 8–12ms.
- Set separate burst concurrency ceiling for the summarization pool (2–4 requests/GPU) to avoid head-of-line blocking.

3) Model routing / fallback
- We can configure smart routing: prefer 13B pool for chat; route to 70B when quality flags trigger; automatically fallback to 13B if 70B capacity exhausted. This aligns with your requirement for mixed routing.

4) Validation plan
- For quantization: SE-run A/B tests on your key prompt set. We’ll produce accuracy drift numbers for int8 vs float16 for the chat prompts before commit.

If that all looks good I’ll join Tue 5/4 10am PT and bring an ops-level node-perf readout (latency/throughput by token mix) to make the final sizing concrete.

—
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
